title.zh: 卷三百〇五 列傳第六十四 楊億 晁迥 劉筠 薛映
title.en: Volume 305 Biographies 64: Yang Yi, Chao Jiong, Liu Yun, Xue Ying
title.raw: 卷三百〇五 列傳第六十四 楊億 晁迥 劉筠 薛映 Volume 305 Biographies 64: Yang Yi, Chao Jiong, Liu Yun, Xue Ying

sentences.zh: 楊億，字大年，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Yang Yi, courtesy name Danian, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi, styled Danian, came from Pucheng in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖文逸，南唐玉山令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wenyi was magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yang Wenyi had served as magistrate of Yushan under the Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 億將生，文逸夢一道士，自稱懷玉山人來謁，未幾，億生，有毛被體，長尺餘，經月乃落。

translations.literal: Before Yi was to be born, Wenyi dreamed that a Daoist who called himself the Hermit of Huaiyu came to pay a visit; before long Yi was born, his body covered with hair more than a foot long, which fell off only after a month.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly before Yi's birth, Wenyi dreamed of a Daoist who introduced himself as the Hermit of Mount Huaiyu coming to call. Soon afterward Yi was born with hair covering his body, more than a foot in length, which did not fall away until a month had passed.

sentences.zh: 能言，母以小經口授，隨即成誦。

translations.literal: When he could speak, his mother orally taught him the Minor Classics, and he could recite them at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once he could speak, his mother taught him the Minor Classics by recitation, and he mastered each passage as soon as he heard it.

sentences.zh: 七歲，能屬文，對客談論，有老成風。

translations.literal: At age seven he could compose prose; in conversation with guests he had the bearing of a seasoned man.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could already draft compositions, and when he conversed with guests he carried himself with uncanny maturity.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，年十一，太宗聞其名，詔江南轉運使張去華就試詞藝，送闕下。

translations.literal: Early in the Yongxi reign, at age eleven, Taizong heard his name and ordered the Jiangnan transport commissioner Zhang Quhua to test his literary skill on the spot and send him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongxi era, when he was eleven, Emperor Taizong heard of him and ordered the Jiangnan transport commissioner Zhang Quhua to examine his literary gifts locally and escort him to court.

sentences.zh: 連三日得對，試詩賦五篇，下筆立成。

translations.literal: For three days in succession he was granted audience; he was tested with five poems and rhapsodies, each completed as soon as his brush touched the paper.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted audience three days running and asked to produce five poems and fu compositions, each finished the moment he set brush to paper.

sentences.zh: 太宗深加賞異，命內侍都知王仁睿送至中書，又賦詩一章，宰相驚其俊異，削章為賀。

translations.literal: Taizong was deeply impressed and ordered the chief eunuch Wang Renrui to escort him to the Secretariat; he also composed a poem, and the chief ministers, astonished at his brilliance, trimmed their memorials into congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was deeply impressed and had the chief eunuch Wang Renrui escort him to the Secretariat. Yi also composed a poem of his own, and the chief ministers, astonished at his brilliance, reshaped their memorials into letters of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 翌日，下制曰：「汝方髫齔，不由師訓，精爽神助，文字生知。

translations.literal: The next day an edict was issued: "You are still in childhood, yet without instruction from teachers your spirit is keen and divinely aided, and you know writing by innate gift.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict declared: "You are still a child, yet without formal schooling your mind is keen—as if heaven itself assisted you—and you know the written word as if born to it.

sentences.zh: 越景絕塵，一日千里，予有望於汝也。

translations.literal: You outstrip the scene and leave the dust behind, a thousand li in a day; I have high hopes for you."
translations.idiomatic: You leave the common herd far behind, advancing a thousand li in a single day. I place great hope in you."

sentences.zh: 」即授秘書省正字，特賜袍笏。

translations.literal: " He was at once appointed corrector in the Secretariat and specially granted robe and tablet.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed corrector in the Secretariat and was specially granted court robe and tablet.

sentences.zh: 俄丁外艱，服除，會從祖徽之知許州，億往依焉。

translations.literal: Before long he mourned his father's death; when the mourning ended, his father's cousin Huizhi was prefect of Xuzhou, and Yi went to live with him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his father. When the mourning period ended, his father's cousin Yang Huizhi was serving as prefect of Xuzhou, and Yi went to stay with him.

sentences.zh: 務學，晝夜不息，徽之間與語，歎曰：「興吾門者在汝矣。」

translations.literal: He devoted himself to study day and night without rest; when Huizhi spoke with him in private he sighed and said, "The one who will raise our house is you."
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to study without pause by day or night. When Huizhi spoke with him privately he sighed and said, "You are the one who will restore our family's fortunes."

sentences.zh: 淳化中，詣闕獻文，改太常寺奉禮郎，仍令讀書秘閣。

translations.literal: During the Chunhua reign he went to court and presented writings; he was changed to ceremonial attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was still ordered to study in the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era he went to court and presented his writings. He was promoted to ceremonial attendant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was permitted to continue his studies in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 獻《二京賦》，命試翰林，賜進士第，遷光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: He presented the "Rhapsody on the Two Capitals"; ordered to be examined by the Hanlin Academy, he was granted jinshi status and promoted to vice-director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his "Rhapsody on the Two Capitals," was examined by the Hanlin Academy, was granted jinshi standing, and was promoted to vice-director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 屬後苑賞花曲宴，太宗召命賦詩於坐側；

translations.literal: When the rear garden held a flower-viewing banquet with music, Taizong summoned him and ordered him to compose a poem at his side;
translations.idiomatic: During a musical banquet for flower-viewing in the rear garden, Taizong summoned him and ordered him to compose a poem at his side;

sentences.zh: 又上《金明池頌》，太宗誦其警句於宰相。

translations.literal: he also submitted the "Ode to the Golden Bright Pool," and Taizong recited its striking lines to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: he also submitted his "Ode to the Golden Bright Pool," and Taizong recited its most striking lines to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，苑中曲宴，億復以詩獻。

translations.literal: The next year in the third month, at another musical banquet in the garden, Yi again presented a poem.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the third month, at another musical banquet in the imperial garden, Yi again presented a poem.

sentences.zh: 太宗訝有司不時召，宰相言：「舊制，未貼職者不預。

translations.literal: Taizong wondered why the authorities had not summoned him in time; the chief ministers said, "By old regulation, those without a posted office did not participate."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was surprised that the authorities had not summoned him promptly. The chief ministers explained, "By longstanding rule, those without a formal posting were not included."

sentences.zh: 」即以億直集賢院。

translations.literal: " Yi was at once assigned to duty at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was immediately assigned to duty at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 表求歸鄉里，賜錢十五萬。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to return to his home district and was granted one hundred fifty thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to return to his home district and was granted one hundred fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 至道初，太宗親製九弦琴、五弦阮，文士奏頌者眾，獨稱億為優，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhidao reign Taizong personally made a nine-string zither and a five-string ruan; many literati submitted encomia, but only Yi's was singled out as superior, and he was granted crimson robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhidao era Taizong personally crafted a nine-string zither and a five-string ruan. Many scholars submitted praise pieces, but only Yi's was judged outstanding, and he was granted the crimson robe and fish tally of higher rank.

sentences.zh: 二年春，遷著作佐郎，帝知其貧，屢有沾賚，嘗命為越王生辰使。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, he was promoted to assistant compiler; the emperor knew he was poor and repeatedly bestowed gifts, and once appointed him birthday envoy to the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he was promoted to assistant compiler. The emperor knew he was poor and repeatedly bestowed gifts upon him, and once appointed him birthday envoy to the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 時公卿表疏，多假文於億，名稱益著。

translations.literal: At the time many memorials of high officials borrowed his prose, and his reputation grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many memorials from high officials were drafted with his help, and his reputation grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 真宗在京府，徽之為首僚，邸中書疏，悉億草定。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was in the capital residence, Huizhi was chief staff officer; all documents of the mansion were drafted by Yi.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhenzong was still heir apparent in the Eastern Palace, Huizhi served as his chief staff officer, and Yi drafted all the residence's official correspondence.

sentences.zh: 即位初，超拜左正言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his accession he was promoted by exception to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Zhenzong's accession, Yi was promoted by exception to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 詔錢若水修《太宗實錄》，奏億參預，凡八十卷，而億獨草五十六卷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qian Ruoshui to compile the Veritable Records of Taizong; he memorialized that Yi should participate; the work totaled eighty juan, of which Yi alone drafted fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Qian Ruoshui to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong. He recommended Yi as a participant. The work ran to eighty juan in all, and Yi alone drafted fifty-six of them.

sentences.zh: 書成，乞外補就養，知處州。

translations.literal: When the book was finished he asked for an outside post to support his parents and was made prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished he asked for a provincial post so he could care for his parents and was appointed prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗稱其才長於史學，留不遣，固請，乃許之任。

translations.literal: Zhenzong said his talent lay especially in historical studies and kept him from going; he pressed his request firmly, and only then was he allowed to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong praised his exceptional gift for historical scholarship and refused to let him leave. Yi pressed his request repeatedly, and only then was he permitted to take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 郡人周啟明篤學有文，深加禮待。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture, Zhou Qiming, was devoted to learning and skilled in letters; Yi treated him with deep courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiming, a scholar of the prefecture renowned for learning and literary skill, received Yi’s deepest courtesy and respect.

sentences.zh: 召還，拜左司諫、知制誥，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Left Secretariat Remonstrator and drafter of edicts, and was granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court, appointed Left Secretariat Remonstrator and drafter of edicts, and granted the gold seal and purple robe of high ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，西鄙未寧，詔近臣議靈州棄守之事。

translations.literal: During the Xianping reign the western frontier was unsettled; the court ordered close ministers to deliberate on abandoning the defense of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era, while the western frontier remained unsettled, the emperor ordered his close ministers to debate whether Lingzhou should be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 億上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 「臣嘗讀史，見漢武北築朔方之郡，平津侯諫，以為罷敝中國，以奉無用之地，願罷之。

translations.literal: "Your servant has read history and seen that when Emperor Wu of Han built the northern commandery of Shuofang, the Marquis of Pingjin remonstrated, holding that it would exhaust China to supply a useless region and asking that it be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: "I have read in the histories that when Emperor Wu of Han established the northern commandery of Shuofang, the Marquis of Pingjin remonstrated, arguing that it would exhaust the empire to sustain a worthless region and urging that the project be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 上使辯士朱買臣等發十策以難平津，平津不能對。

translations.literal: The emperor had the debater Zhu Maichen and others raise ten objections to confound Pingjin, and Pingjin could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the debater Zhu Maichen and others raise ten counterarguments to confound the marquis, and he could not answer them.

sentences.zh: 臣以為平津為賢相，非不能折買臣之舌，蓋所以將順人君之意爾。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that Pingjin was a worthy minister and was not unable to refute Maichen's tongue; he was simply accommodating the ruler's intent.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Pingjin was a worthy minister. It was not that he could not refute Zhu Maichen's arguments, but that he chose to align himself with the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 舊稱朔方，地在要荒之外，聲教不及。

translations.literal: Shuofang was so called of old; its land lay beyond the outer marches, where civilizing influence did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang, as it was known in antiquity, lay beyond the outer marches, where the court's civilizing influence did not reach.

sentences.zh: 元朔中，大將軍衛青奮兵掠地，列置郡縣。

translations.literal: In the Yuanshuo era the Grand General Wei Qing took the field vigorously, seized territory, and set up commanderies and counties in array.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanshuo reign period the Grand General Wei Qing campaigned vigorously, seized territory, and established a network of commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 今靈州蓋朔方之故墟，僻介西鄙，數百里間無有水草，烽火亭障不相望。

translations.literal: Present-day Lingzhou is roughly the old site of Shuofang, remote on the western border; for several hundred li there is no water or grass, and beacon towers and frontier posts cannot see one another.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhou today occupies roughly the old ground of Shuofang. It stands remote on the western frontier, and for hundreds of li there is neither water nor pasture; beacon towers and frontier posts cannot even see one another.

sentences.zh: 當其道路不壅，饢饋無虞，猶足以張大國之威聲，為中原之扞蔽。

translations.literal: When its roads were not blocked and supply trains were secure, it could still magnify the great state's prestige and serve as a shield for the central plain.
translations.idiomatic: When its roads were open and supply lines secure, it could still magnify the empire's prestige and serve as a bulwark for the heartland.

sentences.zh: 自邊境屢驚，凶黨猖熾，爵賞之而不恭，討罰之而無獲。

translations.literal: Since the frontier has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile bands have grown rampant; ennobled and rewarded, they show no deference; punished in campaigns, they are not taken.
translations.idiomatic: Since the frontier has been repeatedly alarmed, the hostile bands have grown ever bolder. Honors and rewards win no deference from them, and punitive campaigns yield no captives.

sentences.zh: 自曹光實、白守榮、馬紹忠及王榮之敗，資糧屝屨，所失至多，將士丁夫，相枕而死。

translations.literal: Since the defeats of Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and transport have been lost in great measure, and soldiers and corvée laborers have died piled upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: Since the defeats suffered by Cao Guangshi, Bai Shourong, Ma Shaozhong, and Wang Rong, supplies and transport have been lost on a vast scale, and soldiers and corvée laborers have died in heaps upon the roads.

sentences.zh: 以至募商人輸帛入穀，償價數倍；

translations.literal: Matters have reached the point of recruiting merchants to bring silk in exchange for grain, with reimbursement several times the cost;
translations.idiomatic: Matters have reached the point where merchants are recruited to deliver grain in exchange for silk, with reimbursement several times the market price;

sentences.zh: 孤壤築城，邊民繹騷，國帑匱乏，不能制邊人之命，及濟靈武之急。

translations.literal: fortresses are built on barren soil, frontier people are in constant turmoil, the national treasury is depleted, and the court cannot command the border peoples or relieve the crisis at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: fortresses are raised on barren ground, frontier populations are in constant uproar, the national treasury is exhausted, and the court can neither command the border peoples nor relieve the crisis at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，凶黨逾盛。

translations.literal: Within a few years the hostile bands have grown ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the hostile bands have grown stronger still.

sentences.zh: 靈武危堞，巋然僅存，河外五城，繼聞陷沒。

translations.literal: Lingwu's perilous walls stand alone, barely surviving; the five cities beyond the river have fallen one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu's perilous walls stand alone, barely intact, while the five cities beyond the river have fallen one after another.

sentences.zh: 但堅壁清野，坐食糗糧，閉壘枕戈，苟度朝夕，未粕出一兵，馳一騎，敢與之角。

translations.literal: They only fortify walls and clear the countryside, sit consuming dried grain, close the forts and sleep on their weapons, barely passing day and night, never sending forth a single soldier or rider to dare contest the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison merely fortifies its walls and clears the countryside, consumes stored grain, closes the forts and sleeps on its weapons, barely surviving from day to day, never venturing forth with a single soldier or rider to contest the enemy.

sentences.zh: 此靈武之存無益，明矣。

translations.literal: That holding Lingwu is of no benefit is clear.
translations.idiomatic: It is plain that holding Lingwu serves no purpose.

sentences.zh: 平津所言罷敝中國以奉無用之地，正今日謂也。

translations.literal: What Pingjin said about exhausting China to supply a useless region is precisely what applies today.
translations.idiomatic: What the Marquis of Pingjin said about exhausting the empire to sustain a worthless region applies exactly to our situation today.

sentences.zh: 臣以為存有大害，棄有大利，國家免粟之勞，士卒流離之苦，悉皆免焉。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that to hold it brings great harm, to abandon it great benefit: the state would be spared the labor of grain transport and the soldiers the suffering of displacement—all would be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that retaining it brings great harm while abandoning it brings great benefit. The state would be spared the labor of grain transport and the soldiers the misery of exile—all of which would cease at once.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜、禹，聖之盛者也，地不過數千里，而明德格天，四門穆穆。

translations.literal: Yao, Shun, and Yu were the greatest of sages; their domains were no more than a few thousand li, yet their bright virtue reached heaven and the four gates were serene.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, Shun, and Yu were the greatest of sages. Their domains extended no more than a few thousand li, yet their luminous virtue reached heaven and peace reigned at the four gates.

sentences.zh: 武丁、成王，商、周之明主也，然地東不過江、黃，西不過氐、羌，南不過蠻荊，北不過太原，而頌聲並作，號為至治。

translations.literal: King Wuding and King Cheng were enlightened rulers of Shang and Zhou; yet their lands east did not pass the Yangzi and Yellow River, west did not pass the Di and Qiang, south did not pass the southern barbarians and Jing, north did not pass Taiyuan—and songs of praise arose together, and they were called the age of perfect order.
translations.idiomatic: King Wuding of Shang and King Cheng of Zhou were enlightened rulers, yet their domains eastward did not extend beyond the Yangzi and Yellow River, westward not beyond the Di and Qiang, southward not beyond the southern barbarians and Jing, and northward not beyond Taiyuan—yet songs of praise arose everywhere, and their reigns were hailed as the age of perfect governance.

sentences.zh: 及秦、漢窮兵拓土，肝腦塗地，校其功德，豈可同年而語哉！

translations.literal: When Qin and Han exhausted the armies and expanded territory until brains and guts smeared the ground, compare their merit and virtue—how can they be spoken of in the same breath!
translations.idiomatic: When Qin and Han exhausted their armies in ceaseless expansion until men lay dead across the land, can their merit and virtue be mentioned in the same breath as those sage rulers?

sentences.zh: 昔西漢賈捐之建議棄朱崖，當時公卿，亦有異論，元帝力排眾說，奮乎獨見，下詔廢之，人頌其德。

translations.literal: Formerly in Western Han Jia Yizhi proposed abandoning Zhuya; at the time high officials also had differing views, but Emperor Yuan forcefully rejected the crowd, boldly held his own view, issued an edict to abolish it, and people praised his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Han, Jia Yizhi once proposed abandoning Zhuya. Many high officials disagreed, but Emperor Yuan forcefully rejected the majority, boldly upheld his own judgment, issued an edict to abandon the commandery, and the people praised his wisdom.

sentences.zh: 故其詔曰：「議者以棄朱崖羞威不行，夫通於時變，即憂萬民之饑鋨，危孰大焉。

translations.literal: Hence his edict said: "Critics hold that abandoning Zhuya shames us because our prestige will not prevail. To understand changing times is to worry for the people's hunger—what peril is greater?"
translations.idiomatic: His edict declared: "Critics say that abandoning Zhuya shames us because our authority will not prevail. Yet to grasp the demands of the age is to worry for the people's hunger—what peril could be greater?"

sentences.zh: 且宗廟之祭，凶年不備，況乎避不嫌之辱哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, in years of famine the ancestral sacrifices are not fully provided—how much less should one avoid the shame of a slight loss of territory?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in years of famine even the ancestral sacrifices cannot be fully provided—how much less should we court the far greater shame of exhausting the realm for a distant outpost?"

sentences.zh: 」臣以為類於靈武也，必以失地為言，即燕、薊八州，河湟五郡，所失多矣，何必此為？

translations.literal: " Your servant holds that this parallels Lingwu: if one must speak of lost territory, the eight prefectures of Yan and Ji and the five commanderies of Hehuang have been lost in far greater measure—why fix on this alone?
translations.idiomatic: I believe this case parallels Lingwu. If the argument is loss of territory, the eight prefectures of Yan and Ji and the five commanderies of Hehuang have already been lost in far greater measure—why fix on this one post alone?

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟太祖命姚內斌領慶州，董遵誨領環州，統兵才五六千，悉付以閫外之事，士卒效命，疆埸晏然，朝廷無旰食之憂，疆埸無羽書之警。

translations.literal: Your servant recalls that Taizu appointed Yao Neibin to command Qingzhou and Dong Zunhui to command Huanzhou, each with only five or six thousand troops, yet entrusted them with all affairs beyond the pass; the soldiers gave their lives, the frontier was tranquil, the court had no worry of dining late, and the border had no alarm of urgent dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that Taizu appointed Yao Neibin to command Qingzhou and Dong Zunhui to command Huanzhou, each with only five or six thousand men, yet entrusted them with full authority beyond the passes. The troops gave loyal service, the frontier remained calm, the court had no need to dine late in anxiety, and the border saw no urgent dispatches.

sentences.zh: 臣乞選將臨邊，賜給廩賦，資以策略，許以便宜而行。

translations.literal: Your servant asks that generals be chosen to command the border, granted rations and tax revenue, supplied with strategy, and allowed to act as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that able generals be chosen to command the frontier, granted rations and local revenue, furnished with strategy, and permitted to act on their own discretion as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 儻寇擾內屬，撓之以勁兵，示之以大信，懷荒振遠，諭以賞格，彼則奔潰眾叛，安能與大邦為敵哉？

translations.literal: If the bandits harass those who submit inward, harass them with strong troops, show them great good faith, soothe the distant and stir the far, instruct them with reward scales—then they will flee in rout and the masses will rebel; how could they stand as enemies of a great state?
translations.idiomatic: If the raiders harass those tribes that have submitted, strike them with strong forces, show them the court's good faith, win over the distant peoples, and proclaim rewards—then they will break and flee, their followers will desert them, and how could they stand against a great power?

sentences.zh: 若欲謀成廟堂，功在漏刻，臣以為彼眾方黠，積財猶豐，未可以歲月破也。

translations.literal: If one wishes to plan success in the ancestral hall and achieve merit within the dripping of the clepsydra, your servant holds that their masses are at present cunning and their accumulated wealth still ample—they cannot be broken in a matter of months.
translations.idiomatic: If one hopes to achieve instant success at court, I believe their forces are cunning and their accumulated wealth still ample—they cannot be broken in a matter of months.

sentences.zh: 直須棄靈州，保環慶，然後以計困之爾。

translations.literal: One need only abandon Lingzhou, hold Huan and Qing, and then use stratagem to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: We need only abandon Lingzhou, secure Huan and Qing, and then wear them down by strategy.

sentences.zh: 如臣之策，得驍將數人，提銳兵一二萬，給數縣賦以資所用，令分守邊城，則寇可就擒，而朝廷得以無虞矣。」

translations.literal: According to your servant's plan, with several fierce generals leading ten or twenty thousand elite troops, grants of tax revenue from several counties to supply their needs, and orders to divide and guard the frontier cities, the bandits could be taken and the court would be free of worry."
translations.idiomatic: By my plan, with several able generals leading ten or twenty thousand elite troops, grants of revenue from several counties to supply their needs, and orders to divide forces and hold the frontier cities, the raiders could be brought to bay and the court would be free of concern."

sentences.zh: 景德初，以家貧，乞典郡江左，詔令知通進銀司兼門下封駁事。

translations.literal: Early in the Jingde reign, because his family was poor he asked to administer a prefecture south of the Yangzi; he was ordered instead to direct the Office for Forwarding Memorials and Silver and concurrently handle rebuttal of edicts at the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era, citing poverty at home, he asked to administer a prefecture south of the Yangzi. Instead he was ordered to direct the Office for Forwarding Memorials and concurrently handle rebuttal of edicts at the Gate.

sentences.zh: 時以吏部銓主事前宜黃簿王太沖為大理評事，億以丞吏之賤，不宜任清秩，即封詔還。

translations.literal: At the time the Ministry of Personnel's chief examiner had appointed Wang Taichong, former recorder of Yihuang, as reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review; Yi held that a low clerk was unfit for a pure rank and sealed the edict and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Ministry of Personnel had appointed Wang Taichong, formerly a clerk in the yellow-register office, as reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review. Yi held that a man of such low clerical origin was unfit for a pure office and sealed the edict to return it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太沖補外。

translations.literal: Before long Taichong was given an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang was given an appointment outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄判史館，會修《冊府元龜》，億與王欽若同總其事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice-director of the History Office; when the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was compiled, Yi and Wang Qinruo jointly oversaw the project.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed vice-director of the History Office. When the court undertook the compilation of the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives, Yi and Wang Qinruo jointly directed the work.

sentences.zh: 其序次體制，皆億所定，群僚分撰篇序，詔經億竄定方用之。

translations.literal: Its order, arrangement, and format were all set by Yi; the officials drafted sections in division, and an edict required that after Yi had revised them they might be used.
translations.idiomatic: He determined its overall arrangement and editorial structure. Other officials drafted individual sections, but an edict required that each pass through Yi's revision before it could be adopted.

sentences.zh: 三年，召為翰林學士，又同修國史，凡變例多出億手。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned as Hanlin academician and also to compile the national history jointly; most changes in precedent came from Yi's hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was summoned as Hanlin academician and also appointed to compile the national history. Most revisions of precedent came from his pen.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，加兵部員外郎、戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu reign he was given the additional titles of vice director in the Ministry of War and director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era he received the additional titles of vice director in the Ministry of War and director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五年，以疾在告，遣中使致太醫視之，億拜章謝，上作詩批紙尾，有「副予前席待名賢」之句。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on sick leave, the court sent a palace envoy with the imperial physician to examine him; Yi submitted a memorial of thanks, and the emperor wrote a poem at the foot of the paper with the line "You match my hope of seating worthy men before me."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, while on sick leave, the emperor sent a palace envoy with the imperial physician to attend him. Yi submitted a memorial of thanks, and the emperor wrote a poem at the foot of the paper with the line, "You match my hope of seating worthy men before me."

sentences.zh: 以久疾，求解近職，優詔不許，但權免朝直。

translations.literal: Because of long illness he asked to be relieved of a post near the throne; a gracious edict did not permit it but only temporarily excused him from morning attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Because of prolonged illness he asked to be relieved of his duties at court. A gracious edict refused, but temporarily excused him from morning attendance.

sentences.zh: 億剛介寡合，在書局，唯與李維、路振、刁衎、陳越、劉筠輩厚善。

translations.literal: Yi was upright and aloof, poor at blending in; in the book office he was on close terms only with Li Wei, Lu Zhen, Diao Kan, Chen Yue, Liu Yun, and their circle.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was upright and aloof, ill suited to easy sociability. In the book office he was close only with Li Wei, Lu Zhen, Diao Kan, Chen Yue, Liu Yun, and their circle.

sentences.zh: 當時文士，咸賴其題品，或被貶議者，退多怨誹。

translations.literal: Literati of the time all relied on his judgments of merit; those he criticized often nursed resentment in private.
translations.idiomatic: Literati of the day all sought his judgment of their work, and those he criticized often nursed private resentment afterward.

sentences.zh: 王欽若驟貴，億素薄其人，欽若銜之，屢抉其失；

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo rose rapidly in rank; Yi had always looked down on him, and Qinruo bore a grudge and repeatedly exposed his faults;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo rose rapidly in rank. Yi had always held him in low regard, and Wang bore a grudge, repeatedly exposing Yi's faults;

sentences.zh: 陳彭年方以文史售進，忌億名出其右，相與毀訾。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian was then advancing by selling his literary and historical skills and resented that Yi's fame stood above his; together they slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian was then advancing through literary and historical work and resented that Yi's reputation outshone his own. Together they slandered him.

sentences.zh: 上素重億，皆不惑其說。

translations.literal: The emperor had always valued Yi highly and was not swayed by any of their talk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always held Yi in high regard and was not swayed by their accusations.

sentences.zh: 億有別墅在陽翟，億母往視之，因得疾，請歸省，不待報而行。

translations.literal: Yi had a villa at Yangdi; his mother went to visit it and fell ill; he asked to return home to see her and set out without waiting for a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yi owned a villa at Yangdi. His mother went to visit it and fell ill. He asked permission to return home to see her and set out without waiting for a reply.

sentences.zh: 上親緘藥劑，加金帛以賜。

translations.literal: The emperor personally sealed medicine and added gold and silk as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally sealed medicines for her and added gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 億素體羸，至是，以病聞，請解官。

translations.literal: Yi had always been frail in body; by this time word came of his illness and he asked to resign office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had always been frail. Now word came of his own illness, and he asked to resign his office.

sentences.zh: 有嗾憲官劾億不俟命而去，授太常少卿，分司西京，許就所居養療。

translations.literal: Someone incited a censor to impeach Yi for leaving without awaiting orders; he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with duty at the Western Capital and permitted to convalesce at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Someone prompted a censor to impeach Yi for leaving without awaiting permission. He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with duty at the Western Capital and permitted to convalesce at home.

sentences.zh: 嘗作《君可思賦》，以抒忠憤。

translations.literal: He once composed the "Rhapsody on Whether the Lord May Be Pondered" to express loyal indignation.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed the "Rhapsody on Whether the Lord May Be Pondered" to give voice to loyal indignation.

sentences.zh: 《冊府元龜》成，進秩秘書監。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was completed he was advanced to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was completed, he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七年，病愈，起知汝州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, recovered from illness, he was recalled to serve as prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after recovering from illness, he was recalled to serve as prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 會加上玉皇聖號，表求陪預，即代還，以為參詳儀制副使，知禮儀院，判秘閣、太常寺。

translations.literal: When the sacred title of the Jade Emperor was to be added, he memorialized asking to take part; he was replaced and recalled at once, made deputy commissioner for deliberating ritual regulations, director of the Court of Ritual, and concurrently vice-director of the Imperial Library and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was to add the sacred title of the Jade Emperor, he petitioned to take part in the ceremony. He was recalled at once, appointed deputy commissioner for deliberating ritual regulations, director of the Court of Ritual, and concurrently placed in charge of the Imperial Library and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年冬，拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Tianxi he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Tianxi he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年，權同知貢舉，坐考較差謬，降授秘書監。

translations.literal: The next year he served concurrently as co-director of the examinations; for errors in grading he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served concurrently as co-director of the civil examinations. Because of errors in grading he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，屬行郊禮，以億典司禮樂，未卒哭，起復工部侍郎，令視事。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother's death; when the suburban sacrifice was to be performed, because Yi directed ritual and music he was recalled before the mourning period ended to Vice Minister of Works and ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother. When the suburban sacrifice was due, the court recalled him before the mourning period had ended because he directed ritual and music, restored him as Vice Minister of Works, and ordered him to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 四年，復為翰林學士，受詔注釋御集，又兼史館修撰、判館事，權景靈宮副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again made Hanlin academician, received orders to annotate the imperial collection, and also served as compiler of the History Office and director of its affairs, with concurrent duty as deputy commissioner of the Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was again appointed Hanlin academician, received orders to annotate the imperial literary collection, and also served as compiler of the History Office and director of its affairs, with concurrent duty as deputy commissioner of the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 錄其子紘為太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: His son Hong was enrolled as ceremonial attendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yang Hong was granted appointment as ceremonial attendant in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 億天性穎悟，自幼及終，不離翰墨。

translations.literal: Yi was keen-witted by nature; from youth to the end he never left brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was keen-witted by nature. From childhood to his last day he never set brush and ink aside.

sentences.zh: 文格雄健，才思敏捷，略不凝滯，對客談笑，揮翰不輟。

translations.literal: His prose style was vigorous, his thought swift, scarcely ever halting; conversing and laughing with guests, he wielded the brush without pause.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was vigorous, his thought swift and rarely halting. Even while conversing and laughing with guests he wrote without pause.

sentences.zh: 精密有規裁，善細字起草，一幅數千言，不加點竄，當時學者，翕然宗之。

translations.literal: He was precise and had rules of composition, skilled at drafting in fine script; a single sheet of several thousand characters needed no correction, and scholars of the time all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: He was precise and disciplined in composition, skilled at drafting in fine script. A single sheet of several thousand characters needed no revision, and scholars of the day took him as their model.

sentences.zh: 而博覽強記，尤長典章制度，時多取正。

translations.literal: Moreover he read widely and remembered strongly, especially excelling in statutes and institutions, on which the age often sought his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and remembered with exceptional strength, especially in statutes and institutions, on which contemporaries often sought his judgment.

sentences.zh: 喜誨誘後進，以成名者甚眾。

translations.literal: He delighted in instructing and guiding the younger generation, and many achieved fame through him.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in guiding younger scholars, and many achieved fame through his patronage.

sentences.zh: 人有片辭可紀，必為諷誦。

translations.literal: If someone had even a phrase worth recording, he would recite it in praise.
translations.idiomatic: If someone produced even a single line worth remembering, he would recite it in praise.

sentences.zh: 手集當世之述作，為《筆苑時文錄》數十篇。

translations.literal: He personally collected contemporary writings into several tens of chapters of the Record of Brush-Garden Current Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He personally collected contemporary writings into the Record of Brush-Garden Current Literature, several tens of chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 重交遊，性耿介，尚名節。

translations.literal: He valued friendship, was upright and unyielding by nature, and honored reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He valued friendship, was upright and unyielding by nature, and held reputation and integrity in high regard.

sentences.zh: 多周給親友，故廩祿亦隨而盡。

translations.literal: He often aided relatives and friends, and so his salary and emoluments were spent as fast as they came.
translations.idiomatic: He often gave generously to relatives and friends, and so his salary and emoluments were spent as fast as they arrived.

sentences.zh: 留心釋典禪觀之學，所著《括蒼》、《武夷》、《潁陰》、《韓城》、《退居》、《汝陽》、《蓬山》、《冠鼇》等集、《內外制》、《刀筆》，共一百九十四卷。

translations.literal: He devoted attention to Buddhist scriptures and Chan meditation studies. His works included the collected writings Kuocang, Wuyi, Yingyin, Hancheng, Tuiju, Ruyang, Pengshan, and Guan'ao, as well as Inner and Outer Drafts and Records of the Brush, totaling one hundred ninety-four juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to Buddhist scriptures and Chan meditation. Among his writings were the collected volumes Kuocang, Wuyi, Yingyin, Hancheng, Tuiju, Ruyang, Pengshan, and Guan'ao, along with Inner and Outer Drafts and Records of the Brush—one hundred ninety-four juan in all.

sentences.zh: 弟倚，景德中舉進士，得第三等及第；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi passed the jinshi examination in the Jingde era and was ranked in the third tier of graduates;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi passed the jinshi examination during the Jingde era and placed in the third tier of graduates;

sentences.zh: 以億故，升為第二等。

translations.literal: Because of Yi, he was promoted to the second tier.
translations.idiomatic: On account of Yang Yi, he was elevated to the second tier.

sentences.zh: 億無子，以從子紘為後。

translations.literal: Yi had no son; he took his nephew Hong as his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had no son and adopted his nephew Hong as his heir.

sentences.zh: 弟偉。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wei.

sentences.zh: 弟 偉

translations.literal: Younger Brother Wei
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Wei

sentences.zh: 偉，字子奇，幼學於億。

translations.literal: Wei, courtesy name Ziqi, studied under Yi from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, courtesy name Ziqi, studied under Yang Yi from childhood.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年獻頌，召試學士院，賜進士及第。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi he submitted a eulogy, was summoned for examination at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and was granted jinshi standing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi he submitted a laudatory verse, was summoned for examination at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and was granted jinshi standing.

sentences.zh: 以試秘書省校書郎知衢州龍遊縣，再補蘄州錄事參軍，國子監薦為直講。

translations.literal: Upon trial appointment as collator in the Secretariat he was made magistrate of Longyou County in Qu Prefecture; subsequently he filled the post of registrar in Qi Prefecture, and the Directorate of Education recommended him as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: After a probationary appointment as collator in the Secretariat, he served as magistrate of Longyou County in Qu Prefecture; he was later appointed registrar in Qi Prefecture, and the Directorate of Education recommended him as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉李遵勖守澶州，辟簽書鎮寧軍節度判官事。

translations.literal: The honorary commander Li Zunxu was prefect of Cao Prefecture and recruited him as signing secretary and adjutant on the staff of the Zhenning military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the honorary commander Li Zunxu was prefect of Cao Prefecture, he recruited Wei as signing secretary and adjutant on the staff of the Zhenning military commission.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺丞、知河間縣，再遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and made magistrate of Hejian County, and was later promoted again to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed magistrate of Hejian County, and later promoted again to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 用近臣薦，為集賢校理、通判單州。

translations.literal: On recommendation by a close court official he was made collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and concurrent prefect of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of a close court official, he was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and concurrent prefect of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會巡檢部卒李素合州卒二百餘人，謀殺巡檢使，入鼓角門，州將不敢出。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Su, a soldier under the patrol inspector, joined with more than two hundred garrison soldiers to plot killing the patrol inspector; they entered the drum-and-horn gate, and the prefectural commander dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Su, a soldier under the patrol inspector, joined more than two hundred garrison troops in a plot to kill the patrol inspector. They burst through the drum-and-horn gate, and the prefectural commander did not dare come out.

sentences.zh: 偉挺身往問曰：「若屬何為而反？

translations.literal: Wei stepped forward and asked, "You all—what are you doing in rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Wei stepped forward and demanded, "What are you people doing in rebellion?

sentences.zh: 」俱曰：「將有訴於州，非反也。

translations.literal: They all said, "We mean to appeal to the prefecture; it is not rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: They all replied, "We only wish to lodge a complaint with the prefecture—it is not a rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」偉曰：「持兵來，非反而何？

translations.literal: Wei said, "You come bearing arms—if not rebellion, then what?
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "You come bearing arms—what is that if not rebellion?

sentences.zh: 若屬皆有父母妻子，以一朝忿而欲魚肉之乎？

translations.literal: You all have fathers and mothers, wives and children—would you because of a moment's anger wish to treat them like meat on a chopping block?
translations.idiomatic: Every one of you has parents, wives, and children—would you because of a single fit of anger throw them to slaughter?

sentences.zh: 」悉令投兵，坐籍首惡得十餘人，斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered them all to cast down their weapons; on investigation the ringleaders numbered more than ten, and they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them all to drop their weapons, identified more than ten ringleaders, and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 徙知祥符縣、提點開封府界諸縣鎮公事，權開封府判官，又判三司開拆司，累遷尚書兵部員外郎、同修起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Xiangfu County and commissioner for the affairs of counties and towns within the Kaifeng jurisdiction; he acted as vice prefect of Kaifeng and also served on the Receiving and Disbursement Bureau of the Three Departments, and was promoted in succession to vice minister of the Ministry of War and co-compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Xiangfu County and commissioner overseeing counties and towns within the Kaifeng jurisdiction, acted as vice prefect of Kaifeng, and also served in the Receiving and Disbursement Bureau of the Three Departments. In time he was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of War and co-compiler of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 偉清慎，無治劇才，常秉小笏以朝，知制誥缺，中書以偉名進，仁宗曰：「此非秉小笏者邪？

translations.literal: Wei was pure and cautious, without talent for handling heavy affairs; he often attended court holding a small tablet. When the post of drafter of edicts fell vacant, the Secretariat submitted Wei's name; Emperor Renzong said, "Is this not the man who always holds the small tablet?
translations.idiomatic: Wei was pure and cautious and lacked talent for demanding assignments; he was known for attending court with a small tablet in hand. When the post of drafter of edicts fell vacant, the Secretariat submitted his name. Emperor Renzong said, "Is this not the man who always carries the small tablet?

sentences.zh: 」遂命知制誥。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly appointed drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 權諫院，嘗曰：「諫臣宜陳列大事，細故何足論。

translations.literal: Acting in the Remonstrance Bureau, he once said, "Remonstrating officials ought to set forth great matters; petty affairs are hardly worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: While acting in the Remonstrance Bureau, he once said, "Remonstrating officials should address great affairs of state; petty matters are hardly worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 」然當時譏其亡補。

translations.literal: Yet at the time people mocked him as being of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Yet people at the time mocked him as being of no practical use.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部郎中，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Justice and made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Justice and appointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 祀明堂，遷右司郎中、判太常寺，為群牧使兼侍讀學士，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice in the Bright Hall he was promoted to director of the Right Bureau, given charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, made herd commissioner concurrently with attendant reader, and advanced to vice grand secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall sacrifice he was promoted to director of the Right Bureau and placed in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed herd commissioner concurrently with attendant reader, and advanced to vice grand secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was awarded the title of vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously awarded the title of vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子 紘

translations.literal: Son: Hong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Hong

sentences.zh: 紘，字望之，以蔭歷官知鄞縣，鄞濱海，惡少販魚鹽者，群居洲島，或掠商人財物入海，吏不能禁，紘至，設方略，使識者質惡少船，及歸，始給還，且戒諭之，由是不敢為盜。

translations.literal: Hong, courtesy name Wangzhi, rose through office by inherited privilege and served as magistrate of Yin County. Yin bordered the sea; ruffians who smuggled fish and salt lived in groups on islets, sometimes plundering merchants' goods and fleeing to sea, and officials could not stop them. When Hong arrived he devised a plan: trusted persons would hold in pledge the ruffians' boats, and only when they returned would the boats be restored, along with admonitions; thereby they no longer dared engage in robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, courtesy name Wangzhi, entered office through inherited privilege and served as magistrate of Yin County. Yin lay on the coast, where young ruffians who dealt in illicit fish and salt gathered on offshore islets and sometimes robbed merchants before fleeing to sea; local officials could not stop them. Hong devised a scheme in which trusted men held the ruffians' boats in pledge until they returned, and only then restored them—with a warning. After that they no longer dared turn to piracy.

sentences.zh: 以億文獻，賜進士出身。

translations.literal: On account of Yi's literary contributions he was granted jinshi standing.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of Yang Yi's literary contributions, he was granted jinshi standing.

sentences.zh: 通判越州，知筠州，提點江東刑獄，除轉運、按察使。

translations.literal: He served as vice prefect of Yue Prefecture, prefect of Jun Prefecture, and judicial commissioner of Jiangdong, and was appointed transport and surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Yue Prefecture, prefect of Jun Prefecture, and judicial commissioner of Jiangdong, and was appointed transport and surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江東饑，紘開義倉振之，吏持不可，紘曰：「義倉，為民也，稍稽，人將殍矣。」

translations.literal: Jiangdong suffered famine; Hong opened the charity granaries to relieve it. An official objected that this was impermissible. Hong said, "Charity granaries exist for the people; delay even slightly, and people will starve."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangdong suffered famine, Hong opened the charity granaries for relief. An official objected that this was not allowed. Hong said, "Charity granaries are meant for the people—delay even briefly, and people will starve to death."

sentences.zh: 紘御下急，常曰：「不法之人不可貸，去之，止不利一家爾，豈可使郡邑千萬家俱受害邪？

translations.literal: Hong was stern in governing subordinates and often said, "Lawless men must not be spared; remove them, and only one household suffers harm—how could one allow millions of households throughout the prefecture and counties to be harmed together?
translations.idiomatic: Hong was stern with subordinates and often said, "Lawless men must not be indulged. Remove them, and only one household suffers—how can one let millions of households across the prefecture and counties suffer together?

sentences.zh: 」聞者望風解去，或過期不敢之官。

translations.literal: Those who heard this fled at the mere rumor, and some did not dare take up their posts even after their term had expired.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard of his reputation fled at the first rumor, and some did not dare report to their posts even after their terms had expired.

sentences.zh: 與王鼎、王綽號「江東三虎」。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Ding and Wang Chuo he was called the "Three Tigers of Jiangdong."
translations.idiomatic: Together with Wang Ding and Wang Chuo he was known as one of the "Three Tigers of Jiangdong."

sentences.zh: 坐降知衡州，徙越州。

translations.literal: On account of an offense he was demoted to prefect of Heng Prefecture, then transferred to Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted to prefect of Heng Prefecture and later transferred to Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為荊南轉運使，徙福建，不赴，知湖州，復為江東轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as transport commissioner of Jingnan, was transferred to Fujian but did not go, became prefect of Hu Prefecture, and again served as transport commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport commissioner of Jingnan, was transferred to Fujian but declined to go, was appointed prefect of Hu Prefecture, and again served as transport commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 官至太常少卿，卒。

translations.literal: He reached the office of vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died in office.

sentences.zh: 紘性嚴，雖家居，兒女不敢妄言笑。

translations.literal: Hong was stern by nature; even at home his sons and daughters did not dare speak or laugh without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was stern by nature; even at home his children did not dare speak or laugh without cause.

sentences.zh: 聚書數萬卷，手抄事實，名《窺豹篇》。

translations.literal: He amassed tens of thousands of volumes of books, copied out factual records by hand, and titled the work Glimpsing the Leopard.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed tens of thousands of volumes, copied out factual records by hand, and titled the work Glimpsing the Leopard.

sentences.zh: 晁迥，字明遠，世為澶州清豐人，自其父佺，始徙家彭門。

translations.literal: Chao Jiong, courtesy name Mingyuan, was for generations a native of Qingfeng in Cao Prefecture; from his father Quan onward the family moved its residence to Pengmen.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Jiong, courtesy name Mingyuan, came from a Qingfeng family in Cao Prefecture; from his father Quan onward the family moved its residence to Pengmen.

sentences.zh: 迥舉進士，為大理評事，歷知岳州錄事參軍，改將作監丞，稍遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: Jiong passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; he successively held the post of registrar in Yue Prefecture, was changed to vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and was gradually promoted to palace aide.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review. He successively held the post of registrar in Yue Prefecture, was appointed vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and was gradually promoted to palace aide.

sentences.zh: 坐失入囚死罪，奪二官。

translations.literal: He was punished for a penal error that caused a prisoner to die and was stripped of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for a judicial error that caused a prisoner to die and was stripped of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 復將作丞，監徐、婺二州稅，遷太常丞。

translations.literal: He was restored as vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, supervised tax collection in Xu and Wu Prefectures, and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, supervised tax collection in Xu and Wu Prefectures, and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，用宰相呂端、參知政事李沆薦，擢右正言、直史館。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, on recommendation by the chief councilor Lü Duan and the vice grand councilor Li Hang he was promoted to remonstrance official of the Right and compiler in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, on the recommendation of Chief Councilor Lü Duan and Vice Grand Councilor Li Hang he was promoted to remonstrance official of the Right and compiler in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 獻《咸平新書》五十篇，又獻《理樞》一篇。

translations.literal: He submitted fifty chapters of the New Book of the Xianping Era and also one chapter of The Pivot of Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted fifty chapters of the New Book of the Xianping Era and also one chapter of The Pivot of Governance.

sentences.zh: 召試，除右司諫、知制誥，判尚書刑部。

translations.literal: Summoned for examination, he was appointed remonstrance official of the Right Bureau, drafter of edicts, and given charge of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for examination, he was appointed remonstrance official of the Right Bureau and drafter of edicts, and was placed in charge of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝北征，雍王元份留守京師，加右諫議大夫，為判官，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched north, Prince Yong Yuan Fen remained to guard the capital; Jiong was given the additional title of grand remonstrance official of the Right, served as his adjutant, and was advanced to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched north, Prince Yong Yuan Fen remained to guard the capital. Jiong was given the additional title of grand remonstrance official of the Right, served as his adjutant, and was advanced to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知審官院，為明德、章穆二園陵禮儀使，同修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was placed in charge of the Bureau of Appointments, served as ritual commissioner for the Mingde and Zhangmu imperial tombs, and co-compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was placed in charge of the Bureau of Appointments, served as ritual commissioner for the Mingde and Zhangmu imperial tombs, and helped compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 知大中祥符元年貢舉。

translations.literal: He oversaw the civil examinations in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the civil examinations in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，祀汾陰，同太常詳定儀注，累遷尚書工部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai and the si sacrifice at Fenyin he joined the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in working out ritual regulations, and was promoted in succession to vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai and the si sacrifice at Fenyin he joined the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in drafting ritual regulations, and was promoted in succession to vice minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，還，奏《北庭記》，加史館修撰、知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, on his return he submitted the Record of the Northern Court and was given the additional posts of history compiler and director of the Office for Transmission and Presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, he submitted the Record of the Northern Court on his return and was given the additional posts of history compiler and director of the Office for Transmission and Presentation.

sentences.zh: 獻《玉清昭應宮頌》，其子宗操繼上《景靈宮慶成歌》。

translations.literal: He submitted the Eulogy of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace, and his son Zongcao followed with the Song of Completion for the Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the Eulogy of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace, and his son Zongcao followed with the Song of Completion for the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「迥父子同獻歌頌，搢紳間美事也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Father and son Jiong together presenting songs of praise—this is a fine thing among the gentry."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For father and son Jiong to present songs of praise together is a fine thing among the gentry."

sentences.zh: 史成，擢刑部侍郎，進承旨。

translations.literal: When the history was completed he was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Justice and advanced to chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the history was completed he was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Justice and advanced to chief academician.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方修禮文之事，詔令多出迥手。

translations.literal: At the time the court was undertaking ritual and textual reforms, and many edicts issued from Jiong's hand.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was undertaking ritual and textual reforms, and many edicts issued from Jiong's hand.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜召對，帝令內侍持燭送歸院。

translations.literal: Once he was summoned for a night audience; the emperor ordered a palace attendant to escort him back to the academy bearing a candle.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was summoned for a night audience; the emperor ordered a palace attendant to escort him back to the academy with a candle.

sentences.zh: 方盛暑，為蠲宿直，令三五日一至院；

translations.literal: It being the height of summer, the emperor exempted him from overnight duty and ordered him to come to the academy only once every three to five days;
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer the emperor exempted him from overnight duty and ordered him to come to the academy only once every three to five days;

sentences.zh: 迥辭以非故事，乃聽俟秋還直。

translations.literal: Jiong declined on the grounds that this was not established precedent, and so was permitted to resume regular duty after autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong declined on the grounds that this was not established precedent, and was permitted to resume regular duty after autumn.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎，請分司西京，特拜工部尚書、集賢院學士、判西京留司御史臺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of War, requested a detached post in the Western Capital, and was specially appointed minister of the Ministry of Works, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and supervisor of the Western Capital branch of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of War, requested a detached post in the Western Capital, and was specially appointed minister of the Ministry of Works, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and supervisor of the Western Capital branch of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 賜一子官河南，以就養。

translations.literal: One of his sons was granted an office in Henan so that he might attend to Jiong's support.
translations.idiomatic: One of his sons was granted an office in Henan so that he could remain nearby to care for him.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Jiong was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Jiong was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 居臺六年，累章請老，以太子少保致仕，給全俸，歲時賜賚如學士。

translations.literal: After six years on the Censorate he repeatedly memorialized to request retirement; he retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with full salary, and received seasonal gifts like a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: After six years on the Censorate he repeatedly memorialized to request retirement. He retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with full salary and received seasonal gifts like a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，迥年八十一，召宴太清樓，免舞蹈。

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng era, when Jiong was eighty-one, he was summoned to a banquet in the Taqing Pavilion and exempted from the court dance of obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era, when Jiong was eighty-one, he was summoned to a banquet in the Taqing Pavilion and exempted from the court dance of obeisance.

sentences.zh: 子宗愨為知制誥，侍從同預宴。

translations.literal: His son Zongque was drafter of edicts and attended the banquet together with the other attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongque, then drafter of edicts, attended the banquet together with the other court attendants.

sentences.zh: 迥坐御史中丞之南，與宰臣同賜御飛白大字。

translations.literal: Jiong was seated south of the vice censor-in-chief and, together with the chief ministers, was granted imperial feibai large-character calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was seated south of the vice censor-in-chief and, together with the chief ministers, was granted imperial feibai large-character calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 既罷，所以寵賚者甚厚，進太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended the gifts bestowed in his honor were very generous, and he was advanced to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended the gifts bestowed in his honor were very generous, and he was advanced to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 後復召對延和殿，帝訪以《洪範》雨暘之應。

translations.literal: Later he was again summoned for audience in the Yanhe Hall, and the emperor questioned him about the correspondence of rain and drought in the Hong Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again summoned for audience in the Yanhe Hall, and the emperor questioned him about the correspondence of rain and drought in the Hong Fan.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「比年變災薦臻，此天所以警陛下。

translations.literal: He replied, "In recent years calamities and disasters have come one after another; this is Heaven's way of warning Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In recent years calamities and disasters have come one after another—this is Heaven's way of warning Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 願陛下修飭王事，以當天心，庶幾轉亂而為祥也。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will rectify royal affairs to accord with Heaven's heart, so that disorder may perhaps be turned into good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will rectify royal affairs to accord with Heaven's will, so that disorder may yet be turned into good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」既而獻《斧扆》、《慎刑箴》，《大順》、《審刑》、《無盡燈頌》，凡五篇。

translations.literal: Thereafter he submitted the Axe-and-Screen, the Admonition on Careful Punishment, the Great Accord, the Examination of Punishment, and the Eulogy of the Endless Lamp—five works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he submitted the Axe-and-Screen, the Admonition on Careful Punishment, the Great Accord, the Examination of Punishment, and the Eulogy of the Endless Lamp—five works in all.

sentences.zh: 及感疾，絕人事，屏醫藥，具冠服而卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: When he fell ill he cut off all human contact, refused medicine, put on cap and robes, and died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he cut off all human contact, refused medicine, put on his cap and robes, and died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 罷朝一日，贈太子太保，諡文元。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for one day; posthumously he was awarded the title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for one day. He was posthumously awarded the title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 迥善吐納養生之術，通釋、老書，以經傳傅致，為一家之說。

translations.literal: Jiong was skilled in breath-regulation and the arts of nurturing life; he was versed in Buddhist and Daoist writings and, by applying the classics and commentaries, formed a doctrine of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was skilled in breath-regulation and the arts of nurturing life. He was versed in Buddhist and Daoist writings and, by applying the classics and commentaries, formed a doctrine of his own.

sentences.zh: 性樂易寬簡，服道履正，雖貴勢無所屈，歷官臨事，未嘗挾情害物。

translations.literal: By nature he was easygoing, generous, and simple; he followed the Way and walked uprightly, never yielding even to the powerful; in every office he held he never let personal feeling harm others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was easygoing, generous, and unpretentious. He followed the Way and walked uprightly, never yielding even to the powerful, and in every office he held he never let personal feeling harm others.

sentences.zh: 真宗數稱其好學長者。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong repeatedly praised him as a learned elder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong repeatedly praised him as a learned elder.

sentences.zh: 楊億嘗謂迥所作書命無過褒，得代言之體。

translations.literal: Yang Yi once said that the edicts Jiong drafted never went beyond due praise and captured the proper style of imperial drafting.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi once said that the edicts Jiong drafted never exceeded due praise and captured the proper style of imperial drafting.

sentences.zh: 喜質正經史疑義，摽括字類。

translations.literal: He delighted in resolving doubtful points in the classics and histories and in compiling categories of characters.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in resolving doubtful points in the classics and histories and in compiling categories of characters.

sentences.zh: 有以術命語迥，迥曰：「自然之分，天命也。

translations.literal: When someone spoke to Jiong of fate by divination, Jiong said, "One's natural allotment is the mandate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When someone spoke to Jiong of fate by divination, Jiong said, "One's natural allotment is the mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 樂天不憂，知命也。

translations.literal: To rejoice in Heaven and not worry is to know one's fate.
translations.idiomatic: To rejoice in Heaven and not worry is to know one's fate.

sentences.zh: 推理安常，委命也。

translations.literal: To reason calmly and rest in the ordinary is to entrust oneself to fate.
translations.idiomatic: To reason calmly and rest in the ordinary is to entrust oneself to fate.

sentences.zh: 何必逆計未然乎？

translations.literal: Why must one calculate in advance what has not yet happened?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one calculate in advance what has not yet happened?

sentences.zh: 」所著《翰林集》三十卷，《道院集》十五卷，《法藏碎金錄》十卷，《耆智餘書》、《隨因紀述》、《昭德新編》各三卷。

translations.literal: His works included the Hanlin Collection in thirty juan, the Daoist Academy Collection in fifteen juan, the Record of Fragmented Gold from the Dharma Storehouse in ten juan, and the Remaining Writings of Elder Wisdom, Records Following Causes, and the New Compilation of Manifest Virtue, each in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included the Hanlin Collection in thirty juan, the Daoist Academy Collection in fifteen juan, the Record of Fragmented Gold from the Dharma Storehouse in ten juan, and the Remaining Writings of Elder Wisdom, Records Following Causes, and the New Compilation of Manifest Virtue, each in three juan.

sentences.zh: 子宗愨。

translations.literal: His son Zongque.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongque.

sentences.zh: 子 宗愨

translations.literal: Son: Zongque
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zongque

sentences.zh: 元昊反，關中久宿師，以宗愨安撫陝西，與夏竦議攻守策。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, troops had long been stationed in Guanzhong; Zongque was sent to pacify Shaanxi and discussed offensive and defensive strategy with Xia Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, troops had long been stationed in Guanzhong. Zongque was sent to pacify Shaanxi and discussed offensive and defensive strategy with Xia Song.

sentences.zh: 未還，道拜右諫議大夫、參知政事。

translations.literal: Before he returned he was appointed on the road grand remonstrance official of the Right and vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he returned he was appointed on the road grand remonstrance official of the Right and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷以金飾胡床及金汲器賜唃廝羅，宗愨曰：「仲叔於奚辭邑請繁纓，孔子曰：『不如多與之邑。

translations.literal: It happened that the court was about to bestow on Gusiluo a gold-inlaid folding chair and gold vessels for drawing water. Zongque said, "Zhongshu and Shuxiang declined a fief from Xi and asked instead for the tasselled bridle ornaments. Confucius said, 'It would be better to give them more fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the court was about to bestow on Gusiluo a gold-inlaid folding chair and gold vessels for drawing water. Zongque said, "Zhongshu and Shuxiang declined a fief from Xi and asked instead for the tasselled bridle ornaments. Confucius said, 'It would be better to give them more fiefs.

sentences.zh: 』繁纓，諸侯之馬飾，猶不可與陪臣，況以乘輿之器賜外臣乎？

translations.literal: The tasselled bridle ornaments are horse trappings of feudal lords and still may not be given to a minister of another state—how much less may one bestow the vessels of the imperial carriage on a foreign subject?
translations.idiomatic: The tasselled bridle ornaments are horse trappings of feudal lords and still may not be given to a minister of another state—how much less may one bestow the vessels of the imperial carriage on a foreign subject?

sentences.zh: 必欲優其禮，不若加賜金帛。

translations.literal: If one must honor him with special treatment, it would be better to add gifts of gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: If the court wishes to honor him with special treatment, it would be better to add gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 」後從帝郊祠感疾，數求罷，除資政殿學士、給事中。

translations.literal: Later, while accompanying the emperor on a suburban sacrifice he fell ill, repeatedly requested dismissal, and was appointed academician of the Hall of Assembled Governance and recipient of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while accompanying the emperor on a suburban sacrifice he fell ill, repeatedly requested dismissal, and was appointed academician of the Hall of Assembled Governance and recipient of edicts.

sentences.zh: 數日，卒。

translations.literal: Within several days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Within several days he died.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書，諡文莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded the title of minister of the Ministry of Works and given the posthumous name Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title of minister of the Ministry of Works and given the posthumous name Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 宗愨性敦厚，事父母孝，篤於故舊，凡任子恩皆先其族人。

translations.literal: Zongque was generous and sincere by nature, filial toward his parents, and devoted to old friends; whenever offices were granted by hereditary privilege he always put his clansmen first.
translations.idiomatic: Zongque was generous and sincere by nature, filial toward his parents, and devoted to old friends. Whenever offices were granted by hereditary privilege he always put his clansmen first.

sentences.zh: 在翰林，一夕草將相五制，褒揚訓戒，人得所宜。

translations.literal: While in the Hanlin Academy, in one night he drafted five edicts for ministers and chief councilors, each with praise, instruction, and admonition suited to the recipient.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Hanlin Academy, in one night he drafted five edicts for ministers and chief councilors, each with praise, instruction, and admonition suited to the recipient.

sentences.zh: 嘗密詔訪邊策，陳七事，頗施用之。

translations.literal: Once by secret edict he was consulted on frontier strategy; he set forth seven points, many of which were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Once by secret edict he was consulted on frontier strategy. He set forth seven points, many of which were put into practice.

sentences.zh: 劉筠，字子儀，大名人。

translations.literal: Liu Yun, courtesy name Ziyi, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun, courtesy name Ziyi, was a native of Daming.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為館陶縣尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Guantao County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Guantao County.

sentences.zh: 還，會詔知制誥楊億試選人校太清樓書，擢筠第一，以大理評事為秘閣校理。

translations.literal: On his return it happened that an edict ordered the drafter of edicts Yang Yi to test candidates in collating books in the Taqing Pavilion; Yun was ranked first and was appointed collator in the Secret Archive with the rank of judicial reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: On his return an edict ordered the drafter of edicts Yang Yi to test candidates in collating books in the Taqing Pavilion. Yun was ranked first and was appointed collator in the Secret Archive with the rank of judicial reviewer.

sentences.zh: 真宗北巡，命知大名府觀察判官事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong toured the north he was ordered to serve as surveillance adjutant of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong toured the north he was ordered to serve as surveillance adjutant of Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自邊鄙罷兵，國家閑暇，帝垂意篇籍，始集諸儒考論文章，為一代之典。

translations.literal: After military operations on the frontier ceased, the state enjoyed leisure; the emperor turned his attention to books and records and first gathered scholars to examine and discuss literature, forming the canon of an age.
translations.idiomatic: After military operations on the frontier ceased and the state enjoyed a period of peace, the emperor turned his attention to books and records. He first gathered scholars to examine and discuss literature, forming the canon of an age.

sentences.zh: 筠預修圖經及《冊府元龜》，推為精敏。

translations.literal: Yun participated in compiling local gazetteers and the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives; he was praised as sharp and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Yun helped compile local gazetteers and the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives and was regarded as exceptionally sharp and diligent.

sentences.zh: 真宗將祀汾睢，屢得嘉雪，召筠及監察御史陳從易崇和殿賦歌詩，帝數稱善。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong was about to sacrifice at Fen and Sui, auspicious snow fell repeatedly; he summoned Yun and Supervising Censor Chen Congyi to compose celebratory songs and poems in Chonghe Hall, and the emperor repeatedly praised them.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Zhenzong prepared to perform sacrifices at Fen and Sui, timely snows fell again and again. He summoned Yun and Supervising Censor Chen Congyi to compose celebratory songs and poems in Chonghe Hall, and repeatedly praised their work.

sentences.zh: 車駕西巡，又命筠纂土訓。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession toured west, he again ordered Yun to compile territorial gazetteers.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's western tour, he again ordered Yun to compile territorial gazetteers.

sentences.zh: 是時四方獻符瑞，天子方興禮文之事，筠數上賦頌。

translations.literal: At that time the four quarters presented omens and portents; the Son of Heaven was then promoting ritual and literary affairs, and Yun repeatedly submitted fu and eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the regions sent in auspicious omens, and the emperor was promoting ritual and literary projects. Yun submitted many fu compositions and eulogies.

sentences.zh: 及《冊府元龜》成，進左正言、直史館、修起居注。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was completed, he was promoted to Left Rectifier, direct appointment in the History Office, and compiler of the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Mirror of the Imperial Archives was finished, he was promoted to Left Rectifier with direct appointment in the History Office and charged with compiling the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 嘗屬疾，予告滿，輒再予，積二百日，每詔續其奉。
