translations.literal: Once when he fell ill, when his granted leave expired he was granted leave again, totaling two hundred days; each time an edict continued his salary.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill on one occasion, each time his medical leave expired he was granted another, until the total reached two hundred days; each extension was accompanied by an edict continuing his salary.

sentences.zh: 遷左司諫、知制誥，加史館修撰，出知鄧州，徙陳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Secretariat Remonstrator and drafter of edicts, added as History Office compiler, sent out as prefect of Dengzhou, and moved to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Secretariat Remonstrator and drafter of edicts, given an additional post as History Office compiler, then sent out as prefect of Dengzhou before being transferred to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，糾察在京刑獄，知貢舉，遷尚書兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: On his return he inspected criminal cases in the capital, supervised the examinations, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he inspected criminal cases in the capital and supervised the civil examinations, then was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 復請鄧州，未行，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: He again requested Dengzhou; before he could depart he was advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to be sent to Dengzhou, but before he could leave he was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 初，筠嘗草丁謂與李迪罷相制，既而謂復留，令別草制，筠不奉詔，乃更召晏殊。

translations.literal: At first Yun had once drafted the edicts dismissing Ding Wei and Li Di from the chancellorship; afterward Wei was kept on, and he was ordered to draft a separate edict. Yun refused the edict, and Yan Shu was summoned instead.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yun had drafted the edicts dismissing Ding Wei and Li Di from the chancellorship. When Wei was retained afterward and Yun was ordered to draft a new edict to that effect, he refused. Yan Shu was summoned to take his place.

sentences.zh: 筠自院出，遇殊樞密院南門，殊側面而過，不敢揖，蓋內有所愧也。

translations.literal: Yun left the Hanlin Academy and met Shu at the south gate of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Shu passed with averted face and did not dare bow—presumably feeling inward shame.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the Hanlin Academy, Yun met Shu at the south gate of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Shu passed with his face turned aside and did not dare bow, evidently ashamed within.

sentences.zh: 帝久疾，謂浸擅權，筠曰：「奸人用事，安可一日居此。

translations.literal: The emperor had long been ill; Wei was gradually monopolizing power. Yun said: "With wicked men holding office, how can one remain here even a day?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been ill for a long time, and Wei was steadily encroaching on power. Yun said, "With wicked men running the government, how can one stay here even one more day?

sentences.zh: 」請補外，以右諫議大夫知廬州。

translations.literal: " He requested an exterior appointment and was made Right Remonstrating Grand Counselor and prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked for a post outside the capital and was appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Counselor and prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷給事中，復召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Yun was transferred to recipient of edicts and again summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong succeeded to the throne, Yun was promoted to recipient of edicts and again summoned as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 逾月，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 先是，三院御史言事，皆先白中丞。

translations.literal: Previously, censors of the three bureaus who wished to speak on affairs would first inform the Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, censors in the three bureaus had to inform the Vice Censor-in-Chief before raising affairs.

sentences.zh: 筠榜臺中：「御史自言事，毋白丞雜知」。

translations.literal: Yun posted a notice in the Censorate: "Censor memorialists shall speak on their own affairs; they need not inform the Vice Censor-in-Chief or the miscellaneous supervisors."
translations.idiomatic: Yun posted a notice in the Censorate: "Censors shall speak on their own affairs and need not first report to the Vice Censor-in-Chief or the miscellaneous supervisors."

sentences.zh: 天聖二年貢舉，數以疾告，進尚書禮部侍郎、樞密直學士、知潁州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng he supervised the examinations; repeatedly taking medical leave, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites in the Secretariat, academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tiansheng era he supervised the examinations. After repeated medical leaves he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites in the Secretariat and academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and was made prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，復知貢舉，進翰林學士承旨兼龍圖閣直學士、同修國史、判尚書都省。

translations.literal: Summoned back, he again supervised the examinations and was promoted to Chief Hanlin Academician, concurrently Direct Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, co-compiler of the National History, and overseer of the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he again supervised the examinations and was promoted to Chief Hanlin Academician, concurrently Direct Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, co-compiler of the National History, and overseer of the Secretariat Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 祀南郊，為禮儀使，請宿齋太廟日，罷朝饗玉清昭應宮，俟禮成，備鑾駕恭謝。

translations.literal: When sacrificing at the Southern Suburb he served as ritual commissioner and requested that on the day of fasting in the Imperial Ancestral Temple the court breakfast at Yujing Zhaoying Palace be suspended, and that after the rite was completed the imperial procession be prepared for the thanksgiving ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At the Southern Suburb sacrifice he served as ritual commissioner. He requested that on the day of fasting in the Imperial Ancestral Temple the court suspend its breakfast at Yujing Zhaoying Palace and that, once the rite was complete, the full imperial procession be prepared for the thanksgiving ceremony.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 筠素愛廬江，遂築室城中，構閣藏前後所賜書，帝飛白書曰「真宗聖文秘奉之閣」。

translations.literal: Yun had long loved Lujiang; he therefore built a residence in the city and constructed a pavilion to store books granted to him over time. The emperor wrote in flying-white script: "Pavilion for Treasuring Zhenzong's Sacred Writings."
translations.idiomatic: Yun had always loved Lujiang. He built a house in the city and a pavilion to store the books the emperor had bestowed on him over the years. The emperor inscribed its name in flying-white script: "Pavilion for Treasuring Zhenzong's Sacred Writings."

sentences.zh: 再知廬州，營塚墓，作棺，自為銘刻之。

translations.literal: Again serving as prefect of Luzhou, he prepared his tomb and grave, made his coffin, and personally carved an inscription on it.
translations.idiomatic: When he served again as prefect of Luzhou, he prepared his tomb and grave, had his coffin made, and carved the inscription himself.

sentences.zh: 既病，徙於書閣，卒。

translations.literal: Once ill, he was moved to the book pavilion and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, he was moved to his book pavilion, where he died.

sentences.zh: 筠，景德以來，居文翰之選，其文辭善對偶，尤工為詩。

translations.literal: From the Jingde era onward Yun stood among the foremost in literary service; his writing excelled in parallel prose, and he was especially skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jingde era onward Yun ranked among the leading literary officials. His prose excelled in parallel composition, and he was especially accomplished as a poet.

sentences.zh: 初為楊億所識拔，後遂與齊名，時號「楊劉」。

translations.literal: At first he was recognized and promoted by Yang Yi; afterward he came to equal him in fame, and the age called them "Yang and Liu."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi had first recognized and promoted him, and Yun later rose to equal fame; contemporaries called them the "Yang-Liu" school.

sentences.zh: 凡三入禁林，又三典貢部，以策論升降天下士，自筠始。

translations.literal: In all he entered the Forbidden Grove three times and three times headed the Examination Bureau; using policy essays to rank scholars throughout the empire began with Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy three times and three times directed the Examination Bureau. Using policy essays to rank scholars nationwide began with him.

sentences.zh: 性不苟合，遇事明達，而其治尚簡嚴。

translations.literal: By nature he would not compromise casually; in affairs he was clear-sighted, and in administration he valued simplicity and strictness.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he would not compromise for convenience. In public affairs he was clear and practical, and in administration he favored simplicity and strictness.

sentences.zh: 然晚為陽翟同姓富人奏求恩澤，清議少之。

translations.literal: Yet in his later years he memorialized on behalf of a wealthy man in Yangzhai of the same surname to seek imperial favor; pure critics thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his later years he memorialized on behalf of a wealthy Yangzhai clansman to obtain imperial favor, and men of upright reputation thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 著《冊府應言》、《榮遇》、《禁林》、《肥川》、《中司》、《汝陰》、《三入玉堂》凡七集。

translations.literal: He authored seven collections: Responses from the Imperial Archives, Honored Encounters, Forbidden Grove, Feichuan, Central Bureau, Ruyin, and Three Entries to the Jade Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He authored seven collections: Responses from the Imperial Archives, Honored Encounters, Forbidden Grove, Feichuan, Central Bureau, Ruyin, and Three Entries to the Jade Hall.

sentences.zh: 一子蚤卒，田廬沒官。

translations.literal: One son died young; his fields and houses were forfeited to the state.
translations.idiomatic: His only son died young, and his fields and houses were seized by the state.

sentences.zh: 包拯少時，頗為筠所知。

translations.literal: When Bao Zheng was young he was well regarded by Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Bao Zheng won Yun's notice and esteem.

sentences.zh: 及拯顯，奏其族子為後，又請還所沒田廬云。

translations.literal: When Bao Zheng rose to prominence he memorialized to have a clansman's son made Yun's heir, and also requested the return of the forfeited fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: After Bao Zheng achieved distinction, he memorialized to appoint a clansman's son as Yun's heir and asked that the confiscated fields and houses be restored.

sentences.zh: 薛映，字景陽，唐中書令元超八世孫，後家於蜀。

translations.literal: Xue Ying, courtesy name Jingyang, was an eighth-generation descendant of Tang Chief Councilor Yuanchao; his family later settled in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying, courtesy name Jingyang, was an eighth-generation descendant of the Tang chief councilor Xue Yuanchao; his family later settled in Shu.

sentences.zh: 父允中，事孟氏為給事中。

translations.literal: His father Yunzhong served the Meng regime as recipient of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yunzhong served the Meng regime of Later Shu as recipient of edicts.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，為尚書都官郎中。

translations.literal: After submitting to the Song he served as Director in the Ministry of Justice of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting to the Song dynasty he served as Director in the Ministry of Justice of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 映進士及第，授大理評事，歷通判綿、宋、昇州，累遷太常丞。

translations.literal: Ying passed the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; he successively served as supervisory prefect of Mian, Song, and Sheng prefectures and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Ying passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review. He served successively as supervisory prefect of Mian, Song, and Sheng prefectures and rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王化基薦為監察御史、知開封縣。

translations.literal: Wang Huaji recommended him as Supervising Censor and magistrate of Kaifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huaji recommended him for appointment as Supervising Censor and magistrate of Kaifeng County.

sentences.zh: 太宗召對，為江南轉運使，改左正言、直昭文館，為江、淮、兩浙茶鹽制置副使。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong summoned him for audience and made him transport commissioner for Jiangnan; he was changed to Left Rectifier, direct appointment in the Zhaowen Library, and Deputy Commissioner for Tea and Salt in Jianghuai and the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong summoned him for audience and appointed him transport commissioner for Jiangnan. He was then made Left Rectifier with direct appointment in the Zhaowen Library and deputy commissioner for tea and salt in Jianghuai and the two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 改京東轉運使，徙河東，兼河西隨軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to transport commissioner for Jingdong, moved to Hedong, and concurrently served with the army in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner for Jingdong, then to Hedong, where he also served with the army on the Hexi frontier.

sentences.zh: 求便親，知相州。

translations.literal: He requested a post convenient for caring for his parents and was made prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a posting that would let him care for his parents and was made prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 再領漕京東，積遷尚書禮部郎中，擢知制誥，權判吏部流內銓兼制置群牧使。

translations.literal: Again he headed transport duties in Jingdong; through repeated promotions he became Director of Rites in the Secretariat, was promoted to drafter of edicts, and temporarily oversaw the Ministry of Personnel's inward selection bureau while concurrently serving as commissioner for the horse herds.
translations.idiomatic: He again headed transport duties in Jingdong and rose through repeated promotions to Director of Rites in the Secretariat. He was then promoted to drafter of edicts, temporarily oversaw inward selection at the Ministry of Personnel, and concurrently served as commissioner for the horse herds.

sentences.zh: 同梁顥安撫河北，還，權判度支。

translations.literal: Together with Liang Hao he pacified Hebei; on his return he temporarily oversaw the Department of Fiscal Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Liang Hao in pacifying Hebei, and on his return temporarily oversaw the Department of Fiscal Affairs.

sentences.zh: 映以右諫議大夫知杭州。

translations.literal: Ying served as Right Remonstrating Grand Counselor and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was appointed Right Remonstrating Grand Counselor and prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 映臨決蜂銳，庭無留事。

translations.literal: When Ying presided over cases his judgments were sharp as a hornet's sting; nothing remained pending in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's courtroom judgments were swift and fierce; no case lingered on his docket.

sentences.zh: 轉運使姚鉉移屬州：「當直司毋得輒斷徒以上罪。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Yao Xian sent a dispatch to subordinate prefectures: "The duty office must not on its own decide exile and heavier crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Yao Xian notified the subordinate prefectures: "The duty office must not on its own decide exile and heavier crimes.

sentences.zh: 」映即奏：「徒、流、笞、杖，自有科條，苟情狀明白，何必繫獄，以累和氣。

translations.literal: " Ying immediately memorialized: "Exile, banishment, beating with rod, and beating with stick each have fixed statutes; if the facts are clear, why imprison and burden harmony?
translations.idiomatic: " Ying immediately memorialized: "Exile, banishment, rod blows, and stick blows each have fixed statutes. When the facts are clear, why keep people in prison and undermine good order?

sentences.zh: 請詔天下，凡徒流罪於長吏前對辨，無所異，聽遣決之。

translations.literal: I request an edict to the empire that wherever exile and banishment crimes are argued before the chief official without dispute, judgment may be pronounced and they may be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an edict go out to the empire: wherever exile and banishment cases are argued before the chief local official without dispute, let sentence be pronounced at once and the offender dispatched.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷施用其言。

translations.literal: " The court adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 與鉉既不協，遂發鉉納部內女口及鬻銅器抑取其直，又廣市綾羅不輸稅。

translations.literal: As he and Xian were already incompatible, he then exposed that Xian had taken in female servants within his circuit and sold bronzeware while withholding full payment, and had bought silk broadly without paying tax.
translations.idiomatic: Already at odds with Xian, he then exposed Xian for taking in female servants within his circuit, selling bronzeware while withholding full payment, and buying silk on a large scale without paying taxes.

sentences.zh: 真宗遣御史臺推勘官儲拱劾鉉，得實，貶連州文學。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong sent Investigation Officer Chu Gong of the Censorate to impeach Xian; the charges were substantiated, and Xian was demoted to Literary Instructor of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong sent Censorate investigator Chu Gong to impeach Xian. The charges were substantiated, and Xian was demoted to literary instructor at Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 映坐嘗召人取告鉉狀，當贖金，帝特貰之。

translations.literal: Ying was liable because he had once summoned someone to obtain an indictment against Xian and should have paid a redemption fine; the emperor specially remitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was technically liable for having once had someone obtain an indictment against Xian and should have paid a redemption fine, but the emperor specially remitted the penalty.

sentences.zh: 在杭五年，入知通進銀臺司兼門下封駁事。

translations.literal: After five years at Hangzhou he entered court as director of the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace, concurrently handling remonstrance and rejection under the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in Hangzhou he returned to court as director of the Office for Transmission and the Silver Terrace, with concurrent charge of remonstrance and rejection under the Gate.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，為東京留守判官，遷給事中、勾當三班院，出知河南府。

translations.literal: When Mount Tai was enfeoffed he served as adjutant to the Eastern Capital garrison commissioner; he was promoted to recipient of edicts, put in charge of the Three-Bureau Office, and sent out as administrator of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mount Tai enfeoffment rite he served as adjutant to the Eastern Capital garrison commissioner. He was promoted to recipient of edicts, placed in charge of the Three-Bureau Office, and sent out as administrator of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰還，駐蹕西京，以映有治狀，賜御書嘉獎。

translations.literal: Returning from the sacrifice at Fenyin, the emperor halted at the Western Capital; because Ying's record of governance was strong, he bestowed an imperial inscription in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the Fenyin sacrifice, the emperor halted at the Western Capital and, impressed by Ying's record of governance, bestowed an imperial inscription in commendation.

sentences.zh: 映好學有文，該覽強記，善筆劄，章奏尺牘，下筆立成。

translations.literal: Ying loved learning and had literary talent; he read broadly and remembered powerfully; he was skilled with the brush—in memorials, letters, and notes he finished as soon as he set pen to paper.
translations.idiomatic: Ying loved learning and wrote well. He read widely and remembered easily, and was adept with the brush: memorials, letters, and notes flowed from his hand at once.

sentences.zh: 為治嚴明，吏不能欺。

translations.literal: In governing he was clear and strict; clerks could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with clarity and strictness, and his clerks could not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 每五鼓冠帶，黎明據案決事，雖寒暑，無一日異也。

translations.literal: Every day at the fifth drum watch he put on cap and sash; at dawn he sat at the desk to decide affairs—whether in heat or cold, not one day differed.
translations.idiomatic: Every day at the fifth watch he dressed for office, and at dawn he sat at his desk to decide cases. Heat or cold, he never varied the routine by a single day.

sentences.zh: 子耀卿，秘閣校理。

translations.literal: His son Yaoqing was collator in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yaoqing served as collator in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 孫紳，直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: His grandson Shen held direct appointment in the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shen held direct appointment in the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自唐末詞氣浸敝，迄於五季甚矣。

translations.literal: Discussion: From late Tang the tone of writing gradually decayed, until by the Five Dynasties it had become extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: From the late Tang the quality of literary style steadily declined, and by the Five Dynasties it had sunk to its lowest point.

sentences.zh: 先民有言：「政厖土裂，大音不完，必混一而後振。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "When government is chaotic and the land is split apart, the great music is incomplete; only after unification can there be revival.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "When government is chaotic and the realm is torn apart, the great music cannot be whole; only after unification can it flourish again.

sentences.zh: 」宋一海內，文治日起。

translations.literal: " Once Song unified the realm within the Four Seas, literary governance rose day by day.
translations.idiomatic: " Once the Song unified the realm, literary culture revived day by day.

sentences.zh: 楊億首以辭章擅天下，為時所宗，蓋其清忠鯁亮之氣，未卒大施，悉發於言，宜乎雄偉而浩博也。

translations.literal: Yang Yi was first to dominate the realm through literary composition and was honored by the age; surely his spirit of pure loyalty and upright candor, not fully deployed before death, all poured forth in his words—no wonder his style was lofty and vast.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi was the first to dominate the literary world and became the age's model. The pure loyalty and upright forthrightness he could not fully put into action in office all poured out in his writing—so it is no wonder his style was grand and expansive.

sentences.zh: 劉筠後出，能與齊名，氣象似爾，至於文體之今古，時習使然，遑暇議是哉。

translations.literal: Liu Yun emerged later yet could match him in fame, and his spirit was similar; as for whether the literary style is ancient or modern, custom of the times makes it so—how could one spare leisure to judge right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun came later yet rose to equal fame, and his spirit was much the same. Whether a style is ancient or modern is simply a matter of prevailing fashion—who has leisure to quibble over it?

sentences.zh: 晁迥寬易，與物無忤，父子先後典書命，稱為名臣。

translations.literal: Chao Jiong was easygoing and tolerant, at peace with all men; father and son successively held charge of edicts and were called eminent ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Jiong was broad-minded and easy in manner, never at odds with others. Father and son in succession held charge of imperial edicts and were acclaimed as eminent ministers.

sentences.zh: 薛映學藝、吏術俱優，而挾忿以抉人之私，君子病之。

translations.literal: Xue Ying was outstanding in both scholarship and bureaucratic skill, yet he nursed resentment to expose others' private failings—men of virtue faulted him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying excelled in both learning and administrative skill, yet he used personal grievances to expose others' secrets, and men of principle criticized him for it.
